title: Do Things that Don't Scale
title_zh: 做那些无法规模化的事情
paragraphs_en: One of the most common types of advice we give at Y Combinator is to do things that don't scale. A lot of would-be founders believe that startups either take off or don't. You build something, make it available, and if you've made a better mousetrap, people beat a path to your door as promised. Or they don't, in which case the market must not exist.

Actually startups take off because the founders make them take off. There may be a handful that just grew by themselves, but usually it takes some sort of push to get them going. A good metaphor would be the crank that car engines had before they got electric starters. Once the engine was going, it would keep going, but there was a separate and laborious process to get it started.
The most common unscalable thing founders have to do at the start is to recruit users manually. Nearly all startups have to. You can't wait for users to come to you. You have to go out and get them.
paragraphs_zh: 在 Y Combinator（Y Combinator），我们最常给出的建议之一就是去做那些无法规模化的事情。很多准创始人相信，初创公司要么起飞，要么就不会。你做出一个产品，把它推向市场，如果你做了一个更好的捕鼠器，人们就会如约而至。如果没有，那就说明市场不存在。
实际上，初创公司之所以起飞，是因为创始人推动它们起飞。也许有少数几家是自然增长的，但通常需要某种推力才能启动。一个好的比喻是汽车发动机在有电动启动器之前的手摇曲柄。一旦发动机运转起来，它就会持续运转，但启动它是一个单独且费力的过程。
创始人在早期最常需要做的无法规模化的事情，就是手动招募用户。几乎所有初创公司都必须这样做。你不能等着用户主动找上门来。你必须走出去找到他们。
